newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU Commission ponders GMO labelling dilemma.
newsitem.headline: EU Commission ponders GMO labelling dilemma.

text.p: The European Commission has begun work intended to calm unease over the use of unlabelled gene-altered products in food, treading a fine line between all-out labelling and possible damage to industry.

A European Commission official, who asked not to be named, said on Tuesday that draft proposals doing the rounds within the EU executive were aimed at clearing up confusion related to EU food labelling laws and various others governing the release and use of genetically modified organisms (GMOs).
"Something is being prepared which might get through the Commission before the end of May," the official said.
The file has been passed to the Commission's secretariat general, rather than to any individual commissioner, to have the proposal drawn up "without any turf fighting going on".

The implication is that any one of the European commissioners for agriculture, consumers, industry, the environment and trade has too many competing concerns to be able to bring the proposal through to adoption by the Commission.

At the proposal's heart is the question of whether the EU should mandate the labelling of food and food ingredients which may contain GMOs or stick to its existing policy that labels should indicate risk or discernible differences between GMO products and their non-GMO equivalents.

"Are we backing the line that we warn for potential risks or are we coming to the line that any product that contains GMOs or may contain GMOs, whether that should be labelled as such?" the official asked, without following up with an answer.

European environmental groups and various retail, wholesale and consumers' organisations have called for the latter in the wake of rows about EU market approval for gene-modified soybeans sold by U.S. chemical company Monsanto 's and for a gene-maize now sold by Switzerland's Novartis.
"We have always said that the label should be there in order to warn the consumer of a potential risk as with additives. Are we now telling them what the production process is?

"That is of course a very difficult option because science, technology and industry move forward and there are those who say that the GMO issue involves one of the few promising industries we have," the official said.

"These are general ideas which have been put into the pipeline and all the Commission services have been invited to give their coments and on that basis a final paper will be prepared," the official added.
